sentences: That 6000 speed on your RAM box?
Your PC probably isn't using it.
New memory starts at a safe default speed set by an industry standard.
The faster number on the box is a profile stored on the stick itself.
It's a tested overclock, and your PC won't use it until you turn it on.
Open your BIOS, find the XMP or EXPO setting, pick the profile, and save.
Then check the memory speed in Task Manager.
If your PC starts crashing, switch it back off.
Full video: Every PC Component Explained, on the channel.
